question.text: The first Persian invasion of Greece was led by this Persian ruler in order to punish them for their participation in the Ionian Revolt. This man divided his empire into satraps.
question.clue: Near the end of his life, he ordered a large limestone rock to be inscribed with his genealogy in three languages; that inscription was translated into English in 1849.

swap.leadin: A military operation in this country called Operation Eagle Claw was authorized only when Secretary of State Cyrus Vance took a brief vacation and was not present to oppose the plan.
swap.text: Name this country that took 52 Americans hostage in 1979 and released them moments after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as President in 1981.
swap.clue: The Constitutional Revolution led to the creation of this country's parliament, the Majlis, and ultimately led to the downfall of its Qajar dynasty.

question.text: The losing forces and Issus and Gaugamela were led by a ruler of this name, though he supposedly fled out of fear at both battles. Another ruler of this name fathered Xerxes the Great, and was Cyrus the Great's nephew.
question.answerHtml: Darius [accept Darius III or Darius the Great or Darius I]
question.clue: One figure of this name faced off against generals like Parmenio and had one of his underlings, Bessus, attempt a coup against him.

swap.text: Leonidas' 300 Spartans were defeated by this empire's much larger force: over 2 million troops if you believe Herodotus, which scholars don't. Xerxes [zerk-zees] led this empire against the Greeks, but was defeated at the naval Battle of Salamis.
swap.clue: A ruler of this empire was assassinated by Artabanus, the commander of this empire's royal bodyguard, the Immortals.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the general Belisarius.
question.text: At the Battle of Dara, Belisarius defeated forces under this empire, who were known for their heavy armored horsemen called cataphracts. Later, the Byzantine Empire established the Eternal Peace with its leader Khosrau I (KHOO-shuh-roo "the first").
question.clue: One king of this dynasty was crowned in utero, while another may have either flayed the skin of a noted captive or poured molten gold down his throat after forcing him and his army to work on an aqueduct, the Band-e-Kaisar.

swap.leadin: After the Iberian War in 532, this empire signed the Perpetual Peace with a neighbor to its west.
swap.text: Name this empire whose leader Khosrow I signed that treaty. Procopius, a neighboring empire's most famous historian, recorded that the treaty was broken within a decade in the Lazic War.
swap.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

question.text: This Elamite city served as the capital of Cyrus the Great before Xerxes' father Darius I built a new one at Persepolis.
question.clue: A polity that called itself Haltamti transferred its capital from Anshan to this city, and this "great holy city" suffered a brutal sack by Ashurbanipal.

swap.leadin: This man named 16 cities after his father, Antiochus.
swap.text: Name this general who served under a famous Macedonian king during his Asian campaigns. He was also the first ruler of a namesake empire, the easternmost of the Macedonian successor states.
swap.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the tribe known as the Alans, who migrated to Europe in the late 4th and early 5th centuries.
question.text: In the 1st century, the Alans raided this empire during the reign of its Vologases I. This empire's cavalry pioneered a tactic where they would feign retreat before turning their bodies to shoot arrows at pursuing adversaries.
question.clue: This empire's namesake "shot" consisted of turning around on horseback during retreat to fire at the advancing army.

swap.text: By dethroning his grandfather Astyages, Cyrus ended this empire, which was led from Ecbatana. Under Cyaxares, this empire took part in the conquest of Neo-Assyria.
swap.clue: As a result of a battle at the Halys River, that waterway was declared its border with Lydia.

question.leadin: A ruler with this name had the Lakhmid king Al Nu'man III executed.
question.text: Give this name of a Sassanid shahanshah who then annexed the Lakhmid kingdom. An earlier shahanshah of this name went to war with Justinian after his allies raided the Lakhmids, who were then Sassanid vassals.
question.answerHtml: Khosrau [accept Khosrau I, Khosrau II, Khosrau Anushirawan, Khosrau the Just, or Chosroes]
question.clue: The second Sassanid ruler with this name held a truce with the Byzantine Empire because of his friendship with the Emperor Maurice, which lasted until Maurice was killed. The first began an "Eternal Peace" because of a bribe from Justinian, which lasted until that ruler got bored.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the generals who carved up Alexander the Great's empire after his death, the Diadochi.
swap.text: This man managed to grab the lion's share of the empire, taking Mesopotamia, Persia, and Bactria. He later fought an unsuccessful war with Chandragupta Maurya.
swap.clue: This ruler, one of Alexander the Great's successors, who established a namesake Hellenistic kingdom in western Asia and was succeeded by his son Antiochus I.

question.text: The Behistun inscription is written in Old Persian, Babylonian, and the language of these peoples, whose capital was Susa. This civilization's Old dynasties included the Awan, Simashki, and Epartid.
question.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

swap.text: Many Neo-Hittite states to the south spoke this Semitic language that replaced Akkadian to become the lingua franca of the Near East
swap.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

question.text: This Sassanid city was the site of an A.D. 363 battle that took place between Shapur II and Emperor Julian, which saw a tactical victory for the Romans. It was the primary capital for both the Parthian and Sassanid Empires.
question.clue: This city was known by Arabs as "al- Mada'in" or "the cities" due to its many suburbs, one of which was sarcastically dubbed "better than Antioch," while another was home to the patriarch of the Nestorian church.

swap.text: The Parthian ruling dynasty was named after this founding ruler, who ruled from the city of Nisa after he conquered a satrapy from the anti-Seleucid rebel Andragoras.

question.leadin: George Rawlinson re-read Strabo's claim that these people required that men must have at least five wives as a misinterpretation of a limit on the size of their harems.
question.text: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg quipped that what people's short-lived empire "exists for us because Herodotus said it did," referencing the historian's questionable accounts of kings like Deioces and Astyages?
question.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

swap.text: Later in his reign, Sargon defeated and exiled this ruler who founded Ecbatana and, per Herodotus, was the first king of the Medes.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a kingdom in Asia FTPE.
question.text: Ecbatana was the capital of this kingdom, which was absorbed into Cyrus the Great's budding Persian Empire around 550 B.C.
question.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

swap.leadin: Name these people or battles important in Cyrus' establishment of the Persian Empire, FTP each.
swap.text: Cyrus began his conquest by overthrowing this Median king, the son of Cyaxares, and, according to Herodotus, Cyrus' grandfather.
swap.clue: The son of Cyaxares and grandfather of Cyrus the Great, he ruled as the last king of the Medes until Cyrus overthrew him.
